summary.text: A 53-year-old man with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, recent pneumonia, severe nutritional compromise (BMI 17.8 kg/m², NRS 2002 score 4) and rectal prolapse (3 months of prolapse sensation after defecation, concentric prolapse about 6 cm; defecography showing complete prolapse) was evaluated with pulmonary function testing, pelvic MRI and chest CT.

After the pulmonary infection was controlled he underwent an Altemeier procedure under spinal anesthesia on January 1, 2024. On January 2 cough, sputum and chest tightness with new infectious CT changes were treated as COPD exacerbation with intravenous meropenem and levofloxacin; methylprednisolone was given for dyspnea and bronchospasm.

On January 5 rectal bleeding and posterior rectal wall rupture on examination, with CT bowel distension and gas, indicated anastomotic leakage. Terminal ileostomy and a self-designed double-lumen irrigation-drainage catheter were placed. That evening he developed altered mental status and respiratory distress and was mechanically ventilated; SOFA score was 8; diagnoses included sepsis, presacral infection, respiratory failure and hypoalbuminemia.

Meropenem and linezolid, enteral nutrition, albumin and fresh frozen plasma continued for persistently elevated PCT and CRP, with continuous saline irrigation at about 100 mL/h; markers fell on serial measurements, he became afebrile and CT showed resolved pneumatosis. He was discharged on January 27, 2024, the catheter was removed 1 week later, and at 4 months colonoscopy showed a well-healed anastomosis without stricture and ileostomy reversal was performed.
